public_comment.topic: Thanked planning board for MBTA Communities Act info session (spoken by a board member, not public).
Objected to flying a pride/progressive flag alongside the American flag on town property, calling it divisive.
Commented on the flag's history, then urged the board to appoint Jack Rabbit and Lou Franco to the Council on Aging for their work helping seniors.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, Five Valley Road; member, Master Plan Steering Committee
public_comment.topic: Said the Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum requirement is too high to hold meetings and asked for a joint select board/planning board discussion.
Responded to the earlier flag comments, saying the pride flag is a symbol of inclusion, not division.
Asked for an update on sewer billing, which had been delayed by a vendor software problem, and whether collections are current.

votes.motion: Approve the town's participation in the Hometown Heroes Banner Program.
Appoint Mary Wilson to the Conservation Commission, term to expire June 30, 2028.
Appoint Andrea Bernap and Teddy Ducet to the Conservation Commission, terms to expire June 30, 2028.
Appoint Jane Rabbit and Susan O'Sullivan to the Council on Aging, terms to expire June 30, 2028.
Appoint Lou Franco and John (Jack) Rabbit to the Council on Aging, terms to expire June 30, 2028.
Appoint Brian Vienno to the Public Access Committee, term to expire June 30, 2028.
Authorize the chair to sign the license agreement for 21 Main Street on behalf of the select board.
Accept a list of prior meeting minutes (January 2024 through May 2025) subject to submitted revisions.
Enter executive session under MGL c.30 §21A(3) to discuss collective bargaining strategy (NEPBA Local 353), not to reconvene in open session.
votes.outcome: passed, roll call: McCloud aye, Em aye, Moore aye, chair aye

budget_items.what_was_said: The historical commission proposed funding the first banners from its own budget, at no cost to the town.
The program requires an initial order to launch, which the historical commission will pay for.
A conservation commissioner noted she wrote a grant, currently in progress, for planning accessible parking at conservation areas.
The finance director reported total revenue collected through the third quarter against the annual projection.
Investment income was reported far above its estimate, attributed partly to market conditions and a new diversified investment policy.
State aid categories, including Chapter 70 school aid, were reported at about three-quarters collected for the year.
Local receipts were reported above estimate overall, with school departmental revenue running well above its estimate.
Total expenditures through the third quarter were reported as most of the annual budget, consistent with prior years.
The elections line ran over this year because of a major election but was offset by a state reimbursement.
The town manager said the program's grant funds ran out over the winter, halting sand deliveries; it will be re-promoted in the fall.
The town proposed a nominal license fee with the neighboring property owner to cover an existing ramp encroachment ahead of a possible easement article.
The board asked for a future readout on ARPA fund status, expected at the next meeting.
A resident asked whether delayed sewer bills, caused by a vendor software transition, have gone out and been collected; the town manager could not confirm collection status on the spot.

decisions.decision: Town manager to notify the Parks Commission about the possible sale of 222 West Townsend Road (recreational land), which other boards had already been asked about.
FY26 select board/town manager goal setting deferred until the full board is present.
Board to keep developing the sick leave bank policy language, including how an appeals process (possibly handled in executive session) would work, once union feedback is complete.
Tax investigation report discussion held over again; assessor to present on directives and next steps at the July 1st meeting.
Board to continue trying to schedule a site walk of 56 Carter Road.

minutes.headline: Select Board filled contested seats on Conservation Commission, Council on Aging, and PAC; approved a Main St. license deal.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard public comment on flying a pride flag, then interviewed and appointed multiple volunteers to the Conservation Commission, Council on Aging, and Public Access Committee, approved the Hometown Heroes Banner Program and a $1 license agreement for a Main Street ramp encroachment, and reviewed the FY2025 Q3 financial report. No new-fiscal-year budget figures, deficits, or cuts were discussed; the board deferred several policy items (goal setting, sick leave bank, tax investigation report) and entered executive session on collective bargaining.

ARPA fund status readout expected at the board's next meeting

what_happened.line: The Select Board filled multiple open seats on the Conservation Commission, Council on Aging, and Public Access Committee, each by unanimous vote.
The board approved a license agreement letting the chair sign off on an existing ramp encroachment at 21 Main Street, ahead of a possible easement article.
The board reviewed the FY2025 third-quarter financial report, including revenue, state aid, and expenditure status, without voting on any figures.
Several policy items were deferred, including FY26 goal setting, a sick leave bank policy, and a standing tax investigation report.
Public comment included a dispute over flying a pride flag on town property, with no board action taken.

why_it_matters: The new Conservation Commission, Council on Aging, and Public Access Committee members will shape decisions on permitting, senior services, and public access/cable matters through mid-2028 terms.
The Main Street license agreement addresses a property encroachment ahead of a possible future town meeting article on a permanent easement.
The sick leave bank policy and tax investigation report remain open items that residents may see return to a future agenda before any vote.
